blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Accuracy, consistency and transparency, at senior level, are not just bookkeeping virtues. They are strategic disciplines that determine whether a board can actually trust the numbers it uses to decide. A company whose principles drift under pressure may look efficient for a quarter — and then discover, in a bad quarter, that the decisions made during the good one were based on figures nobody can quite defend.

The senior leader's job is to protect the principles precisely when they become inconvenient. When a big deal would look better under a slightly aggressive interpretation, the principle is that we do not stretch. When a comparison would look cleaner if one rule changed mid-year, the principle is that we do not change. When a difficult number would be easier to hide, the principle is that it is disclosed.

These moments are never glamorous. They are, however, the difference between companies whose numbers stay trusted across cycles and companies whose numbers are believed only until the first hard test.

items.q: According to the text, why are accuracy, consistency and transparency described as strategic disciplines?
options: They determine whether a board can trust the numbers it decides on
They reduce the cost of preparing the accounts
They allow figures to be restated whenever convenient
They impress external auditors during a bad quarter
items.why: "strategic disciplines that determine whether a board can actually trust the numbers it uses to decide."

items.q: When is the senior leader's job to protect the principles?
options: Precisely when the principles become inconvenient
When the numbers are already favourable
Only at the end of the financial year
When the auditors are watching
items.why: "to protect the principles precisely when they become inconvenient."

items.q: The text suggests that a company whose principles drift under pressure…
options: may look efficient briefly but leaves undefendable decisions behind
will avoid difficult decisions altogether
will be praised for its flexibility across cycles
always fails within a single quarter
items.why: Inferência: "may look efficient for a quarter — and then discover… decisions… based on figures nobody can quite defend."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Trusted numbers must survive more than one cycle
Transparency has strategic value at board level
Bending a principle for one strong quarter is a sensible trade-off
A difficult number should be disclosed rather than hidden
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta contra esticar princípios por um bom trimestre.

items.q: What does "believed only until the first hard test" imply about such companies?
options: Their numbers are never questioned by anyone
They disclose more than their competitors
Their credibility collapses as soon as conditions turn difficult
They pass every audit with ease
items.why: Inferência: a confiança nesses números é frágil e não resiste ao primeiro momento difícil.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte numa reunião de fechamento trimestral. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before we vote on this, I want to be very clear about what is actually being proposed. We are being asked to reclassify a major operating expense so that it sits below the line this quarter. Yes, the numbers look cleaner today. But let me tell you what happens next quarter.

Next quarter, that same cost reappears somewhere unfamiliar, the comparison no longer holds, and the first analyst who models this properly asks why. And we will not have a clean answer, because there isn't one. The only reason to move it is that it flatters the current print.

I'm not questioning anyone's motives here. Under pressure, a small reinterpretation always feels reasonable. That is precisely why it's dangerous. If we stretch this one, we have quietly told the whole finance team that the rule bends when the quarter is tight.

So my recommendation is simple. We leave the expense where it belongs, we disclose the pressure it puts on the quarter, and we take the hit honestly. A trusted number in a bad quarter is worth far more than a tidy one nobody can defend.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What exactly is Charlotte responding to?
options: A plan to change the company's auditors
A request to delay the quarterly close
A proposal to cut the finance team's budget
A proposal to reclassify a major operating expense to improve this quarter
items.why: "We are being asked to reclassify a major operating expense so that it sits below the line this quarter."

items.q: According to Charlotte, what happens next quarter if the expense is moved?
options: The board reverses the decision automatically
The auditors approve it without comment
The comparison breaks and an analyst asks why
The cost disappears permanently
items.why: "the comparison no longer holds, and the first analyst who models this properly asks why."

items.q: What does Charlotte say is the ONLY reason to move the expense?
options: It simplifies the audit process
It flatters the current print
It complies with a new accounting rule
It reduces the company's tax bill
items.why: "The only reason to move it is that it flatters the current print."

items.q: Why does Charlotte call the reinterpretation "dangerous" even though it feels reasonable?
options: Because it would take too long to implement
Because it would increase costs elsewhere
Because it signals to the whole team that the rule bends when the quarter is tight
Because the auditors have already rejected it
items.why: Inferência: "we have quietly told the whole finance team that the rule bends when the quarter is tight."

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's stance?
options: Indifferent to how the quarter is reported
Enthusiastic about the reclassification
Accusing her colleagues of bad faith
Firm on the principle while sparing people's motives
items.why: Inferência: "I'm not questioning anyone's motives" — ela separa a pessoa do princípio, mas não cede.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "When principles drift under pressure, the numbers slowly stop meaning the same thing." Here, to drift means to…
options: be formally rewritten by the board
move away gradually from a fixed standard
collapse suddenly and visibly
become stricter over time
items.why: To drift = desviar, afastar-se aos poucos de um padrão fixo.

items.q: "We do not stretch a rule just because a big deal would look better." To stretch a rule means to…
options: interpret it beyond its honest limits
apply it to a new subsidiary
abolish it entirely
explain it more clearly
items.why: To stretch = esticar: forçar a interpretação além do que ela honestamente comporta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A difficult number is easier to hide, but the principle is that it must be ___."
options: disclosed
deferred
discounted
duplicated
items.why: To disclose = divulgar; o princípio da lição é revelar o número difícil, não escondê-lo.

items.q: "The best test of a principle is whether it survives an aggressive interpretation." An aggressive interpretation is one that…
options: ignores the rule completely
follows the rule as conservatively as possible
pushes a rule as far as possible in your favour
is rejected by the auditors on sight
items.why: Aggressive interpretation = interpretação agressiva: leva a regra ao limite a seu favor.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Trusted numbers stay believed across ___; tidy-looking ones are believed only until the first hard test."
options: cycles
quarters alone
auditors
disclosures
items.why: Cycle = ciclo; a lição contrasta números que resistem aos ciclos com os que não resistem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em discussões de fechamento e princípios contábeis. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Charlotte pushed back on the reclassification." To push back on means to…
options: resist or challenge it
postpone reading it
rewrite it overnight
approve it without comment
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The audit committee still has to sign off on the treatment." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve it
delay it indefinitely
leak it to the press
comment on it informally
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Moving the expense will not move the needle on the underlying business." This means it will…
options: not make a real, noticeable difference
double the reported profit
attract regulatory attention
take several quarters to measure
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não faz.

items.q: "We agreed the principle in January but never followed through on it." They…
options: documented it in great detail
failed to carry it through to completion
changed it halfway through the year
delegated it to the auditors
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's not paper over a difficult number to protect the quarter." To paper over something means to…
options: escalate it to the regulator
print extra copies for the board
resolve it permanently
conceal a problem instead of resolving it
items.why: Paper over = disfarçar um problema em vez de resolvê-lo — o oposto de disclose.
